correctness_confidence.basis: Hand-rechecked: identity (3) for the squared residual, Mathieu expansion E(L)=-L+sqrt(L/2)-1/16 from a0(2L)/4, Gaussian ratio 1/8, cubic (16) from (17), Lemma 4/5/Prop 6 chain, Cor 9. No error found. Asymptotic uniformity in Thm 3 and Appendix A (not re-derived in full) rest on dense, unchecked estimates.

rigor.basis: Core chains are explicit and mostly checkable, and limits are honestly stated. But Thm 2 uses a non-quantified implicit-function neighborhood and eps_0 is non-effective; Prop A.5 constants only bind for n>~1e21; the dense Lemma A.1/A.3/A.5 estimates and the Thm 3 lower-bound uniformity are compressed and hard to verify fully.

novelty.basis: Removes the log factor of Tan et al. (exp(-(1+o(1))sqrt(n) log n)) to exp(-C sqrt(n)), and gives the sharp 1/sqrt8 circle-root barrier plus a one-interior-zero collapse. Novelty relies on arXiv 2026 preprints I could not check; priority search is admittedly non-exhaustive. Methods are largely adaptations.

significance.basis: Solid, specialized contribution to residual bounds for Schur-stable polynomials and exterior power sums; the sharp circle barrier and the exact zero-count threshold are clean. Does not settle optimal rates (disk, one-root) and the Erdos 973 answer was already known, so impact is moderate and narrow.

reproducibility.basis: Proofs are written out, appendix added, explicit parameters given. Supplementary scripts and numerical checks are described but were not available to me and I ran nothing. Non-effective constants (M_A, C_A, N_A) and the references (arXiv 2026) limit independent reproduction.

summary: The paper proves lim s_n = lim r_n = 1/sqrt8 for polynomials with all zeros on the unit circle (Mathieu ground state lower bound, explicit family for the upper bound), shows one interior zero suffices for vanishing residual O(n^{-1/6}), a fixed number of interior zeros gives superalgebraic decay, and a universal disk lower bound exp(-C sqrt n), C>sqrt((8/3)log 17). I rechecked the key identities and the Mathieu and Gaussian computations and found no error, but did not verify every appendix estimate, and no code was run. Main caveats are non-effective constants and unverifiable external citations.
strengths: Sharp, explicit circle-root limit 1/sqrt8 with matching upper and lower arguments
Exact threshold (zero vs one interior zero) with explicit parameters in the one-root case
Elementary finite certificate giving explicit bound exp(-3 sqrt n) for n>=10^4
Candid statement of what is not proved (optimal rates, effectiveness, priority)
weaknesses: Theorem 2 relies on a non-quantified implicit-function neighborhood; M_A, C_A, N_A are non-effective
Appendix constants in Prop A.5 give non-trivial bounds for the one-root family only for n of order 1e21 or more
Lower and upper disk bounds differ greatly (exp(-C sqrt n) vs n^-A); optimal rates open
Novelty and priority depend on 2026 arXiv preprints and are not exhaustively searched
Several dense asymptotic arguments (Thm 3 uniformity, Lemma A.1(e)) are compressed
potential_errors: Thm 3 lower bound: uniform control of the Mathieu remainder on the window lambda=n/2+O(sqrt n) is argued briefly; the O(q^{-1/2}) uniformity is imported from DLMF
Lemma 4 requires sqrt(n+1)e^{-y}<=1 and eta>0; the parameter regime for n>=10^4 is checked only by sketched numerics (log 17<3, monotonicity of gamma_n/sqrt n)
Lemma A.3(ii) bound f''>=-8 Sigma_2 and the tau_1 integral lower bound are stated tersely
strong_novelty_candidates: Removal of the log n factor in the exponent for restricted residual lower bound (exp(-C sqrt n))
Sharp circle-root residual limit 1/sqrt8 and exact interior-zero-count threshold
